summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' challenge at START Hack Munich: analyze Soony's launch data, then build a deployed product that detects hidden supply problems, grounds them in source documents, and acts through supplier emails, voice, and routines, while staying general beyond Soony.
summary.outcome: Found that Collector's Edition (art books, failed statues, packing speed) and later game cards miss Sunday 20:00 despite the 'all ok' plan. Built a poller/agent/app with Today, Launch (replacing Plan), Routines and Suppliers pages, two-step voice decisions, repeat-based routine offers and generalized site/cutoff naming. Latest Launch page work is committed locally but not yet pushed.

repo: Portal API has only files list, single file and archive.zip; there are no webhooks, so changes must be detected by polling and comparing SHA-256 (files can be replaced under the same name).
Spreadsheets are recognized by columns rather than filenames. A file whose columns change is skipped silently, which is the 'system says fine' trap.
Server runs uvicorn without reload in tmux (ask-soony-app), so backend changes need a manual restart before the UI shows new fields.
Confidential portal data lives in gitignored data/; never commit it, never print tokens, and never approve or accept in tests, because that sends real supplier emails.
Team conventions: ask before every push, commit author josteng, no em dashes, no attribution trailers, no PRs without asking.
Entire hooks only checkpoint when repo files change, so sessions with no file changes show 'skipping checkpoint'.
Voice decisions now require prepare_decision then decide with a one-time token (TOKEN_TTL_S=600, stored in voice_tokens.json).
Soony-specific wording such as 'trucks' (about 30 UI places) and 'Hamburg' remained in the code; the delivery site is now read from sites.csv.

code.finding: The decide tool requires a token and confirmed flag issued by prepare_decision; the token is one-time and bound to card, decision and option.
New module that builds the per-edition and per-part launch data (launch.parts, hours_left) from the verifier's dispatch.json and the packing clock.
build_state() now includes a 'launch' field; the file was concurrently edited, so the two added lines need checking.
New Launch page at /launch replacing Plan; /plan redirects to /launch and /plan?card=X to /d/X.

workflow: Fixed polling loop plus LLM extraction plus plain-code recompute keeps numbers checkable; use agents for reading and acting.
Delegating UI work to subagents that own specific files and sending follow-ups via SendMessage worked, but concurrent edits to shared files (api.py, Today.tsx) needed care.
Verify UI changes with Playwright screenshots against the live app, mocking all non-GET requests so no real actions fire.
A one-off subagent cross-checking all order confirmations and scans against SAP surfaced the key discrepancies.

friction: The portal token was initially empty, which blocked data access until it was supplied.
Voice assistant announced it would outline the action and then decided without confirmation, which showed up as a premature 'Done'.
Three tests broke when decide began requiring a token and had to be rewritten to the two-step flow.
Plan and Today kept overlapping, which took several redesign rounds, and the Flow/Steps/Expanded routine views were redundant.
The user repeatedly rejected cluttered or unprofessional designs.
A stray .vite/ cache folder appeared in the repo root and was left out of commits.
Concurrent builders editing the same files (api.py, Today.tsx) caused coordination overhead.
open_items: About 10 or more local commits on jonas/today-flow are unpushed; the user must approve the push.
Live voice call with a microphone has not been tested end to end, and an email edited on screen then confirmed by voice sends the original draft.
Data-shape warning (column loss, unread new files, suggested renames) is only planned; the server side was to start next and the Launch display is not built.
Replace the remaining 'trucks' wording with a per-customer cutoff label in the UI.
Briefing page and doc still show the 14:00 state, not the 14:37 drop.
Register sender email addresses in the portal Settings so supplier emails can go out.
Decide whether to delete the earlier Claude doc, and how to handle PR #5 versus jonas/today-flow into main.
Write the README, demo script, video (max 3 min) and deck for the Sun 12:00 hand-in.
Remove 'Hamburg' remnants and confirm whether portal data is identical across teams.
Game-card split between editions is unknown on the Launch page, and the Spare figure can differ by about 0.1 h from the slack figure shown elsewhere.
